_about: The 60 gold questions for the BinaSmart banking and money pack (the sector-pack method, design 2026-09-16-airline-travel-design.md section 1.3): 40 Amharic, 20 English, each naming the document under knowledge/banking/ that answers it. `topic` is the English subject the page must discuss, and for a page that is itself in Amharic, `topicAm` is the Amharic one. ops/packs/build-gold.js refuses to write the gold file unless at least three of a topic's content words are in that page's text, so a question can never point at a page that does not talk about it. Questions were written from the pages as they were measured on 2026-09-16, never from memory. Ten of them ask an Amharic question of an Amharic page, which is the first same-language slice in any BinaSmart pack. Seventeen of the sixty were refused on the first run against the fetched pages and were repaired on 2026-09-17: eleven had their label moved to the page that really answers them, six named something no page in the pack answers and were replaced. Every one of the seventeen carries a note saying which, and a replaced question keeps its original wording in question_replaced. BATCH 2 (2026-09-17, Task 15b): thirty more questions - 20 Amharic, 10 English - on the three sources Task 15a added, the National Bank of Ethiopia, telebirr and M-PESA. Fifteen of the twenty Amharic questions are answered by a page that is ITSELF in Amharic, because telebirr publishes 28 Amharic pages; three are deliberately Amharic questions whose only page is English (the National Bank publishes its complaint procedure, its FX rules and its interest-rate directive in English only), so the cross-lingual gap stays measurable rather than being designed away. Every label was verified twice: by ops/packs/build-gold.js --check, and by reading the page body with the rendered header and the disclaimer stripped, because the disclaimer alone can satisfy the three-content-word check. Questions carry batch: 1 or batch: 2 so the benchmark can slice them apart. BATCH 3 (2026-09-17, Task 15c): twenty more questions - 14 Amharic, 6 English - about the directives the National Bank publishes ONLY as photographs of paper, which entered the pack in Task 15c through OCR. They cover the subjects a customer actually asks and the pack could not answer before: the complaint procedure and its time limit and the fee-disclosure duty under FCP/01/2020, fraud reporting under SBB/59/2014, the credit record and how to dispute it under CRB/02/2019, the currency-management directives, the payment-system-operator and payment-instrument-issuer rules under ONPS/02/2020 and ONPS/04/2021, bank licensing and foreign banks and deposits under the Banking Business Proclamation 1360/2025, and customer due diligence under the Money Laundering proclamation. THREE of the fourteen Amharic questions have a gold page that is itself in Amharic - the three currency directives the National Bank wrote in Amharic. The other eleven are Amharic questions whose only page is English, kept rather than dropped because that is the gap this pack keeps measuring, and because the National Bank publishes its consumer-protection, fraud and licensing rules in English only. Every label was verified twice: by ops/packs/build-gold.js --check, and by reading the document body on disk with the rendered header and the disclaimer stripped.

coverage_gaps.subject: published interest rates
coverage_gaps.why: Zemen's rate page is client-rendered and came back thin, so it is not in the pack, and no institution in the pack publishes a lending rate. The only rate figures on disk are deposit rates in Dashen's FAQ and Zemen's business product page.

coverage_gaps.subject: exchange rate board
coverage_gaps.why: No page in the pack carries a buying/selling rate table. Zemen's exchange-rates page was not selected and CBE's is client-rendered.

coverage_gaps.subject: loan calculator
coverage_gaps.why: The word calculator appears in no document in the pack; Zemen's calculator page renders in the browser and came back empty.

coverage_gaps.subject: how to lodge a complaint
coverage_gaps.why: No page tells a customer how to complain. ቅሬታ appears only as a navigation link on zemen-am-home.

coverage_gaps.subject: CBE diaspora accounts
coverage_gaps.why: Only five CBE pages survived the fetch and none of them is about diaspora accounts, so a question naming CBE could not be retargeted.

coverage_gaps.subject: per-question CoopBank FAQ pages
coverage_gaps.why: CoopBank's individual ufaq URLs were not fetched as separate documents; the whole archive arrived as coopbank-ufaqs.

measured.theOneNumberThatMatters: Split the same-language slice and the pack reaches the design target where the language matches. The ten Amharic questions whose gold page is itself Amharic score 90.0% on retrieval and 90.0% as shipped - the 90% the design asked for, met exactly. The twenty English questions on English pages score 80.0% retrieval and 60.0% as shipped. The thirty Amharic questions whose only gold page is English score 30.0% retrieval and 40.0% as shipped. The pack is not bad at Amharic; it is being asked to find English pages with Amharic questions in a corpus where one bank out of six publishes Amharic.
measured.verdict: The target was NOT met and no label was moved to make it look met. Twenty-two of the twenty-seven misses are the retriever returning a different institution's page on the same product, or the same Zemen page in the other language, for a question that names no bank; the gold set can only name one page, so those score zero even though the pack answered. Five are genuine retrieval failures where nothing in the top three answers.
measured.whyAmharicIsWorse: Zemen is the only institution in this pack with an Amharic locale (see sources.json langNote for zemen, dashen, cbe and coopbank). An Amharic question therefore lands on a Zemen Amharic page whatever bank its label names: a zemen-am- page is in the shipped top three for 32 of the 40 Amharic questions when only 10 of them have a zemen-am- gold page, and won rank one in 13 of the 19 Amharic misses. This is not fixable by fetching, because Dashen, CBE and CoopBank do not publish Amharic product pages at all. It is the argument for asking every Ethiopian institution to publish in Amharic, and it is the first time any BinaSmart pack has been able to measure it: 70.0% when the question and its gold page share a language, 40.0% when they do not.
measured.remediesNotApplied: Convention 14 allows four remedies. (a) Retargeting was refused: the plan forbids moving a label to whichever page happened to win, and Task 8 had already moved eleven labels and replaced six questions against the fetched pages. (b) Widening an allow list was refused: every gold page is already in the pack and was verified to contain its answer, so the pack is never missing the answer, and Task 10 is skipped for that reason. (c) The banking PREFER list was measured and left alone: a non-pack document (guide:open-bank-account-ethiopia, guide:telebirr, page:diaspora) is in the shipped top three for 7 of the 27 misses, but the gold page sits at rank 4 in only 3 of them, so removing BinaSmart's own account-opening guide from PREFER could gain at most 3 questions while taking the right answer away from real users. (d) The remaining misses are recorded, here and in the report. The shared reranker, the embedding model, hybridScore and the +0.06 tie-breaker were not touched; the airline gate re-ran at exactly 86.7% retrieval and 83.3% as shipped on the same corpus to prove it.

afterAmharicHeaders.what: Task 10b gave every ENGLISH document of the pack a grounded Amharic title and a two-or-three-sentence Amharic key-fact summary in its header, which is the half of the sector-pack design (an English and Amharic header per document naming the key facts) the pack shipped without. 203 documents, generated by ops/packs/am-headers.js into knowledge/banking/am-headers.json from each page's own text and checked digit by digit against it; 202 got a title and a summary, 1 a title only, 1 summary was refused by the grounding check. No page was re-fetched, no label was moved, and the reranker, the embedding model, hybridScore and the +0.06 tie-breaker were not touched.
afterAmharicHeaders.theOneNumberThatMatters: The slice the Amharic header was written for is the slice that moved: the thirty Amharic questions whose only gold page is English went from 30.0% to 50.0% on retrieval and from 40.0% to 50.0% as shipped, while the ten Amharic questions on Amharic pages held at 90.0%/90.0% and the same-language retrieval slice did not move at all. Four questions net changed hands as shipped (bk-018, bk-019, bk-022, bk-029, bk-038 and bk-043 gained; bk-012 and bk-020 lost), and six of the nine questions the first run classed as amharicLocaleCapture are no longer captured. The gap between asking in the page's own language and asking across languages narrowed from 30 points to 23.3 and is not closed: an Amharic header is not an Amharic page, and the argument for asking every Ethiopian institution to publish in Amharic stands.
afterAmharicHeaders.gatesHeld: The airline pack was not touched by one byte (git status --short knowledge/travel empty, test/packs/airline-identity.test.js green, --rerender reporting 0 of its 114 documents changed) and its benchmark re-ran at exactly 86.7% retrieval and 83.3% as shipped. Dr Afiya and Asmat re-ran on gold-v3-agents at 96.4% retrieval and 98.2% as shipped, question for question identical to the run before this change.
afterAmharicHeaders.cost: The header change re-rendered 203 documents and moved 407 chunks of 1,657 (the header sits in the first section of each document, so only that section re-chunked); the corpus went from 16,117 to 16,155 chunks.

afterBatch2.alsoRun: /root/bini-eval/retrieval-gold-banking-20260917-052005.json — the same run ten minutes earlier, identical in every slice
afterBatch2.what: Task 15b. Thirty questions were added (batch 2: 20 Amharic, 10 English) on the National Bank of Ethiopia, telebirr and M-PESA, the three sources Task 15a folded into the pack, and two batch-1 labels were repaired. No page was re-fetched, no chunk was re-embedded, and the reranker, the embedding model, hybridScore and the +0.06 tie-breaker were not touched. The only production change in the task is that contextFor now prints a Source line — publisher, url, fetch date — at the top of every page block, which the benchmark does not use.

pageAt3.allRetrieval: 71.1% (the 60-question set read 56.7% on this same corpus)

afterBatch2.theOneNumberThatMatters: Batch 2 scores 93.3% and batch 1 scores 61.7% on the same corpus, with the same retriever, in the same run. The difference is not the questions and not the retriever: it is that fifteen of batch 2's twenty Amharic questions have a gold page that is ITSELF in Amharic, because telebirr publishes 28 Amharic pages, while batch 1 has ten such questions out of forty because Zemen is the only bank in the pack with an Amharic locale. The whole-set split says the same thing again: 86.2% when the question and its page share a language, 43.8% when they do not. This is now the second independent measurement of the same finding, and it is the argument for asking every Ethiopian institution to publish in Amharic.
afterBatch2.repairs: Two batch-1 labels were moved, both Amharic questions about receiving money from abroad that name no institution: bk-004 from zemen-am-digital-remittance and bk-028 from dashen-remittance, both to ethiotelecom-am-international-remittance, telebirr's own Amharic page, which answers the receiving side in the language the question is asked in. The other four questions the corpus moved in Task 15a — bk-014, bk-018, bk-021 and bk-050 — keep their labels and their misses, because what outranked them (a telebirr landing page, a law on cheques, the FX directive) does not answer better than the page already named. A label was never moved to whatever happened to win.
afterBatch2.verdict: The design target of 90.0% as shipped is met by batch 2 (93.3%) and not by the pack as a whole (72.2%). The gap is the cross-lingual one, and it is now measured at 34.5 points of retrieval between a question asked of a page in its own language and one asked across languages.
afterBatch2.gatesHeld: Dr Afiya and Asmat re-ran on gold-v3-agents at 96.4% retrieval / 99.1% as shipped, question for question what Task 15a measured (Afiya 96.3/98.1, Asmat 96.5/100.0). The airline pack re-ran at 85.0% retrieval both times it was run; as shipped was 81.7% on the first run and 83.3% on the second, a single question (tv-015) that the live reranker swapped for a sibling check-in page. git status --short knowledge/travel is empty.
